subject: general
question:
**Direction: The following sentence has been split into segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

If I were your mother / I would have taken care / of you and your sisters.
solution:
The correct answer is "No error." [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence appears to be grammatically correct and does not contain any errors.
 
• It is a conditional sentence expressing **a hypothetical situation.**
 
• **"If I were your mother" **this segment uses the correct form of the verb for unreal, hypothetical situations or conditions.
 
• The construction** "would have" + past participle (taken)** is typical for these kind of unreal conditionals.
 
• **"of you and your sisters" **correctly completes the phrase** "taken care of"** which is a common idiom meaning **to look after or be responsible for someone.**

So, the correct answer is Option 3. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

 
• "If I were your mother, I **would have taken **care of you and your sisters."

 
 
• This sentence is an example of a **"mixed conditional"** sentence. It suggests that the speaker is imagining how things might have been different in the past if she had been their mother.
 
 
 
• "If I were your mother, I **would take** care of you and your sisters."
 
 
• This sentence is an example of a **"second conditional"** sentence. It implies **an unreal or hypothetical **situation in the present or future. The speaker is imagining what she would do right now or in the future if she were their mother.
 
 
 
• Both sentences are grammatically correct. The one to use would depend if you're talking about a hypothetical past (with 'would have taken') or a hypothetical present or future (with 'would take').
